sections.title: Evolution and breakdown of chiral anomaly in Weyl semiconductor tellurium
sections.abstract: The authors report tunable negative longitudinal magnetoresistance in doped tellurium, its persistence to ambient temperature, and a reversal under extreme quantum-limit conditions that may indicate an interaction-driven phase transition.
sections.claimed_result: Authors attribute enhanced negative magnetoresistance near the Weyl point to chiral anomaly; the low-temperature sign reversal beyond the quantum limit is presented as a possible field-induced collective state, not a definitive phase transition.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; magnetotransport in doped tellurium under varied Fermi-level and magnetic-field conditions.
sections.unique_caveat: The proposed collective-state interpretation of the extreme-field reversal is tentative; the abstract does not identify a definitive phase diagnosis.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors list a 2026 Communications Physics journal reference (DOI 10.1038/s42005-026-02901-3); the work is cross-listed across materials physics, applied physics, and quantum physics.

sections.title: An entangling Hubbard quasiparticle collider on a digital quantum processor
sections.abstract: The authors collide a doublon and holon in a 21-site Fermi–Hubbard chain encoded on 42 qubits, measure quasiparticle transmission consistent with the Bethe-ansatz result, and infer collision-generated number entanglement.
sections.claimed_result: Authors report the first hardware measurement of Hubbard-model quasiparticle transmission and use particle-number fluctuations to infer entanglement between transmitted and reflected components.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; 21-site/42-qubit Fermi–Hubbard simulation on the ibm_boston processor, compared with the Bethe-ansatz scattering matrix.
sections.unique_caveat: The measured number fluctuations show component weights but do not directly establish coherence between transmitted and reflected branches; the authors identify interference measurements as a possible test.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A direct 42-qubit hardware scattering experiment, cross-listed between quantum physics and strongly correlated electrons, with transmission compared to an exact Bethe-ansatz benchmark.

sections.title: A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of ∼12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift 0∼9 in COSMOS
sections.abstract: Using JWST/NIRCam wide-field slitless spectroscopy across 0.33 square degrees, the authors assemble 12,275 emission-line galaxy spectra over redshifts 0–9, with line fluxes, redshifts, and derived properties.
sections.claimed_result: Authors report a homogeneous sample of 12,275 objects and composite spectra revealing faint hydrogen-recombination, CO-absorption, and Fe II features.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; JWST/NIRCam COSMOS-3D F444W grism data over 3.9–5.1 μm combined with multi-band imaging; typical 3σ line-flux limit 3.2×10⁻¹⁸ erg s⁻¹ cm⁻².
sections.unique_caveat: Slitless-source overlap and frequent single-line spectra create line-identification and redshift ambiguities; some contamination requires additional inspection.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A large JWST spectroscopic catalogue with a stated flux limit and composite spectra spanning cosmic time; the authors say it is submitted to ApJS.

sections.title: Magnetic-field-induced detwinning of orientational domains in altermagnet α-MnTe: A single-crystal neutron diffraction study
sections.abstract: Single-crystal neutron diffraction shows that an in-plane field near 2 T prepares α-MnTe in a nearly single-orientation magnetic-domain state, with a refined domain population of 0.97:0.03:0.
sections.claimed_result: Authors find field-induced selection of a common Néel-vector orientation in α-MnTe and report an ordered Mn moment of 4.62(8) μB at 2 K and 2 T.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; single-crystal neutron diffraction at 2 K and 2 T, with refinement of 61 reflections.
sections.unique_caveat: Unpolarized diffraction cannot distinguish domain repopulation from continuous Néel-vector rotation or resolve time-reversal antiphase domains; authors describe a near-single-orientation, not a true single-domain, state.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Quantitative neutron-diffraction refinement using 61 nuclear and magnetic reflections, including a measured field scale and nearly complete domain-population estimate.

sections.title: Nailing down the Hubble constant value through time delay cosmography: A 3% measurement from SN Refsdal
sections.abstract: The authors infer H₀ = 65.0⁺²·⁰₋₁·⁸ km/s/Mpc from strongly lensed supernova Refsdal, reporting 3.0% precision after adding the host galaxy’s extended surface-brightness data to a cluster-lens model.
sections.claimed_result: Within flat ΛCDM, authors obtain H₀ = 65.0⁺²·⁰₋₁·⁸ km/s/Mpc and Ωm = 0.30⁺⁰·⁰⁸₋₀·⁰⁹, consistent with earlier lensed-supernova results.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; SN Refsdal time delays and 77,000 HST host-galaxy pixels interpreted through cluster-lens mass models.
sections.unique_caveat: The cluster total-mass parameterization is deliberately held fixed; the authors identify lens-mass and time-delay uncertainties as comparable remaining contributors.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A quantitative 3% constraint from a single strongly lensed supernova, four mass-model realizations, and submission to Astronomy & Astrophysics.

sections.title: Determination of U-spin breaking parameters with an amplitude analysis of the decay D⁰→K⁰S,Lπ⁺π⁻
sections.abstract: A BESIII simultaneous amplitude analysis of D⁰→K⁰Sπ⁺π⁻ and D⁰→K⁰Lπ⁺π⁻ measures complex U-spin-breaking parameters using 20.3 fb⁻¹ of e⁺e⁻ collision data at 3.773 GeV.
sections.claimed_result: Authors report fitted U-spin-breaking parameter magnitudes from 0.62 to 4.45, resonant fit fractions, and model predictions for average strong-phase parameters.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; BESIII e⁺e⁻ data collected at √s = 3.773 GeV and analyzed with a simultaneous amplitude fit.
sections.unique_caveat: Average strong-phase parameters are model predictions from the amplitude analysis; interpretation of resonance-specific quantities depends on that model.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A large BESIII collaboration and 20.3 fb⁻¹ sample underpin a simultaneous analysis of both neutral-kaon final states; the dataset is described as substantially larger than in earlier work.

sections.title: Impact of ab initio E1 strength on neutron capture rates along the nickel isotopic chain
sections.abstract: Ab initio electric-dipole strength calculations for nickel isotopes predict enhanced neutron-capture rates relevant to r-process simulations, with the enhancement varying across isotopes and temperature.
sections.claimed_result: Authors report low-lying E1 strength above neutron threshold growing with neutron number and increased calculated capture rates for ⁶⁸–⁷⁸Ni; for ⁸⁰Ni the enhancement begins near 0.5 GK.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; Lorentz-integral-transform coupled-cluster calculations with chiral two- and three-nucleon interactions, propagated into TALYS reaction-rate calculations.
sections.unique_caveat: Uncertainty is dominated by inversion of the integral transform, and most neutron-rich isotopes considered are beyond experimental reach.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across nuclear theory, nuclear experiment, and high-energy astrophysics; calculations are benchmarked against measured ⁵⁸Ni photoabsorption and ⁶⁸Ni E1 strength.

sections.title: Evidence of Taste-Symmetry restoration for Kähler-Dirac fermions on Euclidean Dynamical Triangulations
sections.abstract: In quenched Euclidean Dynamical Triangulations, the authors find Kähler–Dirac fermion mass splittings appear to shrink with lattice spacing, suggesting restoration of the relevant taste symmetry toward the continuum limit.
sections.claimed_result: Authors find unprotected bound-state mass splittings scale down with lattice spacing, suggesting an analogy with staggered fermions in flat-space lattice theories.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; two-particle bound-state spectra in quenched Euclidean Dynamical Triangulations.
sections.unique_caveat: The quenched approximation omits matter back-reaction on geometry, and the continuum-restoration conclusion is an extrapolative interpretation of the observed lattice-spacing dependence.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed between lattice and theoretical high-energy physics; tests a continuum-limit property on fluctuating geometries and compares the breaking scale with emergent de Sitter and Planck scales.
